name: Multi-brand
summary: One shared system with three brands as themes. Components never change; brand primitives do.
description: Multi-brand is an Open DS scheme: a full set of answers to the Open DS grammar, with the reasons behind each, usage rules, voice and tone, and the tokens that follow. One shared system with three brands as themes. Components never change; brand primitives do.

ai.use_when: Companies with several brands or white-label products on one component library.
ai.avoid_when: A single product with one brand: the brand layer is cost with no user.

scenarios.text: A customer signs up for a plan on the Birch site, then manages it in the shared account area.
A product team launches a fourth brand by adding brand primitives, without touching components.

summary.text: A plain shared voice. Each brand adds its own tone on top, never its own structure.

principles.text: Shared structure: object, state, next step.
Brand tone lives in headlines and marketing copy, not in errors.
Errors and confirmations read the same in every brand.

inventory.description: The components this system carries, picked from the grammar catalogue by the components answers. Anything not listed is out.

in.why: The code that verifies an email or phone.
Lays out every form the same way in every brand.
Validation shared by every product team.
The customer in the account menu.
Where a page sits in the account area.
Plans and orders while they load.
Plan details and fee explanations, opened by tap on any device.

out.why: Customers manage plans; they do not analyse data.
Customers browse; keyboard command menus suit experts.
Customers use any device, and on touch screens hover hints never show; a popover explains a fee instead.

samples.description: Sample content for showing this system: written from its use scenarios, in its voice, with every status mapped to a meaning. Storybook, the site and the docs read it; it is never shared between schemes.

usage.use: The closest semantic token, then ask for a new one
usage.not: A raw value or a brand primitive in the component
usage.why: A raw value shows the same in every brand, so it breaks the theme.

usage.use: A shared verb; the brand may choose the headline verb
usage.why: Shared labels keep the account area the same in every brand.

usage.use: Shared across brands: plain and specific
usage.why: Errors read the same in every brand, so support can help anyone.
usage.example: Your card was declined. Try another card or contact your bank.

usage.use: Brand tone allowed: Aster calm, Birch friendly, Coral upbeat
usage.not: The same flat line in every brand
usage.why: Success is a safe moment for brand tone.
usage.example: Aster: Your plan is active. · Birch: You're all set! · Coral: Let's go, your plan is live.

usage.why: The structure is the shared core; words carry the brand.
usage.example: No orders yet. Your first order will appear here.

usage.use: Shared across brands: plain and specific
usage.not: Brand tone when something is lost
usage.why: Loss is never the moment for personality.
usage.example: Cancel your plan? It stays active until the end of the month.

usage.use: Brand tone in the first headline only
usage.why: One headline carries the brand; the rest stays shared.
usage.example: Birch: Hi! Let's set up your plan.

usage.use: a component from the inventory with brand tokens
usage.not: a component made for one brand
usage.why: Brands change primitives, never components; one brand-only part breaks the shared library.

color.$description: Colour options: raw hue ramps. Each hue has a light ramp, a dark ramp (the same steps tuned for dark backgrounds) and its base value ($root). Themes pick from these; components never read them.

slate.$description: The slate hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

teal.$description: The teal hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

purple.$description: The purple hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

orange.$description: The orange hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

green.$description: The green hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

amber.$description: The amber hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

red.$description: The red hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

black.$description: See-through black for scrims behind dialogs, light and dark.

space.$description: Space options. Names give the size in pixels at the default text size; values are rem.

size.$description: Size options for controls, rows and icons.
Type size options. Names are pixels at the default text size; values are rem, so text grows with the user's setting.

1_2.$description: A ratio of the text size.

1_25.$description: A ratio of the text size.

1_3.$description: A ratio of the text size.

1_4.$description: A ratio of the text size.

1_5.$description: A ratio of the text size.

family.$description: Font family options. Each brand's theme picks its display, body, interface and data fonts from these.

fast.$description: Fast: the usual convention for feedback, about 120ms.

moderate.$description: Moderate: a calm, easy-to-follow speed, about 200ms.

relaxed.$description: Relaxed: a slower, springy speed for expressive motion, about 320ms.

shadow.$description: Raw shadows. Elevation semantics point at these.

card.$description: Raw shadow for card in light mode.

overlay.$description: Raw shadow for overlay in light mode.

card-dark.$description: Raw shadow for card in dark mode.

overlay-dark.$description: Raw shadow for overlay in dark mode.

aster.label: Aster
aster.description: Calm and precise: teal, Inter, small corners.

theme.$description: The Aster theme: what each brand-dependent semantic key picks, in light and dark, plus mode-free picks (fonts, corners) in base.

birch.label: Birch
birch.description: Friendly and helpful: violet, Plus Jakarta Sans, soft corners.

theme.$description: The Birch theme: what each brand-dependent semantic key picks, in light and dark, plus mode-free picks (fonts, corners) in base.

coral.label: Coral
coral.description: Upbeat and energetic: coral orange, Poppins, pill controls.

theme.$description: The Coral theme: what each brand-dependent semantic key picks, in light and dark, plus mode-free picks (fonts, corners) in base.

default.$description: Height of buttons and inputs, and the smallest target.

container.$description: Corner of cards, menus and dialogs.

scrim.$description: Dims the page behind a dialog.

focus-ring.$description: Focus ring color on any button.

icon-size.$description: Size of an icon inside a button.

checked.$description: Fill of a checked checkbox or an on switch.

background.$description: Fill of a dialog, menu or toast.

scrim.$description: Color that dims the page behind a dialog.

content.$description: Voice tokens: the words components use for common actions. Text, not CSS.

commit.$description: The label of the action that completes a task.

cancel.$description: The label of the way out next to the main action.

destroy.$description: The label of an action that deletes data.

retry.$description: The label that repeats a failed action.

empty-action.$description: The label of the action in an empty state.
